result:
I would remove the human mind’s ability to turn other people—and the future—into abstractions.

Most of the world's worst tragedies don’t come from pure malice. They come from distance. A person can be fiercely kind to someone crying in front of them and completely unmoved by a million people suffering on the other side of the planet, simply because the mind files distant lives away as statistics. People can love their children deeply and still borrow recklessly from the world those children will inherit, because fifty years from now feels theoretical compared to this afternoon.

I wouldn’t want people overwhelmed by the constant, unfiltered pain of everyone on Earth—that would just cause paralysis. I would simply close that strange gap in perception where it becomes effortless to treat someone else’s reality as less solid than your own.

If distant lives and long-term consequences carried the same quiet, unmistakable weight as the person sitting across from you right now, most of the world's other crises—war, systemic neglect, quiet everyday cruelty, ecological ruin—would begin to unravel on their own. Not because humanity was forced to be good, but because indifference would stop being easy.
